newsitem.title: USA: Labor secretary to contact Teamsters, UPS.
newsitem.headline: Labor secretary to contact Teamsters, UPS.

text.p: Labour Secretary Alexis Herman said she would call the heads of United Parcel Service and its striking Teamsters union Sunday to try to end the weeklong walkout against the largest U.S. package delivery company.
"I plan to do that today," Herman said on the NBC television programme Meet the Press. "I want to find out what it's going to take from them to get these talks moving in the right direction."
But Herman defended President Clinton's refusal for now to invoke a federal law that would let him end the strike if he decides it was threatening the nation's health and safety.
"We don't believe that this situation has reached the state of what we define as a national emergency as it is defined in the Taft-Hartley legislation," she said.
On Saturday, UPS and the International Brotherhood of Teamsters broke off their talks with no reported movement toward a contract and no plan to reconvene.
Federal mediator John Calhoun Wells, who conducted the talks, said the issues were difficult and he would reconvene negotiations when the time was right. He did not say when that might be.
